caveats:
The area of interest is a fixed 1 km buffer around river centrelines. It marks the
corridor under assessment and is not a modelled or observed flood extent.

OpenStreetMap coverage reflects where volunteer mappers have been active and changes
between daily updates. Overture layers combine several upstream sources, some of them
machine generated. Cross-check critical decisions with local field knowledge.
name: hot_flood_npl
notes:
OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps vector layers for the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river
corridor in Bagmati and Gandaki Provinces, Nepal, extracted for the 2026 flash flood
response.

The area of interest is a 1 km buffer around the river centrelines, covering 314.30
square kilometres. It runs from Rasuwagadhi on the China border, down the Bhote Koshi
and Trishuli, to the Narayani confluence at Devghat in Chitwan. It crosses six
districts, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahu and Chitawan, and twenty
municipalities.

The corridor merges two sources: the original partner shapefile for the upper reach and
OCHA's HPCS 1 km corridor for the downstream reach. A small part of the buffer above
Rasuwagadhi falls inside China, where the OpenStreetMap country extract has no coverage.

Every layer is published here as a resource, and most layers carry two versions, one
from OpenStreetMap and one from Overture Maps. The two are not interchangeable:

- **OpenStreetMap** layers are live. They are rebuilt daily from the latest OSM data,
  so they pick up work by volunteer mappers as the response progresses. Use these when
  currency matters.
- **Overture Maps** layers fuse building footprints and other features from Microsoft,
  Google and OpenStreetMap. That fusion gives broader coverage than OSM alone in places
  volunteers have not reached yet, but **Overture is not updated daily**. It follows
  Overture's own release cycle, so it will not reflect mapping done during this response
  and will fall progressively further behind the OpenStreetMap layers.

In short, Overture is wider but older; OpenStreetMap is current. For damage assessment
against the latest mapping, prefer the OpenStreetMap layers and treat Overture as a
supplement where OSM coverage is thin.

Mapping task boundaries from the Tasking Manager campaign are published here too and
refreshed daily, showing where volunteers are being asked to map.

The bridge damage assessment is contributed by [ICIMOD](https://www.icimod.org/),
the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.

- Source: [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/), [Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/), [ICIMOD](https://www.icimod.org/)
- Part of HOT disaster response exports on HDX by [HOT](https://www.hotosm.org/)

resources.description: Bridge damage assessment for the 2026 Trishuli basin flood, compiled by ICIMOD. 33 permanent bridges: 25 washed out, 3 damaged, 5 spared. Includes Miteri Bridge at Rasuwagadhi on the Nepal-China border. Covers Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan districts. 28 of the 33 fall inside the dataset area of interest, 3 lie beyond it and 2 records carry no coordinates, so this layer is not clipped to the corridor. The source `status` field mixes English and Nepali; a normalised `status_en` field is added and the original is preserved unchanged. Source: ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development).

This layer shows where volunteers are being asked to map, which is not the same as where data exists: a project at low completion marks a known gap rather than coverage.
